title: Safe index, set & assert
hints: Each function is the same shape: a named `err` result, a deferred closure that calls `recover()`, then the plain operation (`return s[i], nil`).

Run-time panic values implement `error`. In the closure: `if e, ok := r.(error); ok { err = fmt.Errorf("safe index: %w", e) }` keeps the original value inspectable with `errors.As`. A tiny helper `asError(prefix string, r any) error` avoids repeating this three times.

`StringAt`: `defer func() { if r := recover(); r != nil { s, err = "", asError(fmt.Sprintf("string at %d", i), r) } }()` followed by `return row[i].(string), nil`. The closure can read `i` because it is a parameter of the surrounding function.
